images.note: Mercantilism's 'fixed pile': Spanish silver dollar (piece of eight), the era's bullion coin; 1821 example of the same type (later date, noted honestly).
images.source: Smithsonian Institution, National Museum of American History
images.title: Spanish silver dollar (piece of eight), 1821

images.note: Mercantilism's 'ship raw cheap' job: sugar hogsheads carted aboard vessels, Antigua; Clark 1823, near-contemporary but idealized planter's-eye view.
images.title: Carting and putting sugar-hogsheads on board, Antigua (Clark, 1823, pl. 10)

images.alt_source: Digital Commonwealth / Boston Public Library (Leventhal Map Center)
images.note: Navigation Acts world: Moll's 1715 West-Indies chart marking trade winds and galleon/flota tracts; contemporary with the Acts' operation.
images.title: A map of the West-Indies (Herman Moll, 1715)

images.note: Manufacturing-acts beat (Wool 1699/Hat 1732/Iron 1750): fireback cast at Colebrookdale Furnace, 1763; contemporary colonial iron product of exactly the industry Parliament fenced off.
images.title: Fireback, Colebrookdale Furnace, 1763

images.note: Molasses Act 1733 beat via Maya's own association: Leslie Jones photo of the 1919 Boston molasses-disaster tank cutting; 20th-century photo, honest anachronism, matches the script's named image.
images.title: Cutting the tank with acetylene torch, Molasses Disaster (Leslie Jones, Jan 1919)

images.note: The chain behind the triangle: enslaved laborers cutting cane, Antigua; Clark 1823, near-contemporary but idealized (well-dressed workers, no whip shown).
images.title: Cutting the sugar-cane, Antigua (Clark, 1823, pl. 4)

images.note: Good-deal side of the double-edged sword: the Royal Navy guarding the sea lanes; Monamy 1720-30, contemporary with the salutary-neglect era.
images.title: British Men-of-War and a Sloop (Peter Monamy, 1720-30)

images.note: Customs/duties machinery (Board of Trade 1696, vice-admiralty courts, Molasses Act duties): London Custom House; Rowlandson 1808, later depiction of the same institution.
images.title: Custom House (Thomas Rowlandson, 1808)

images.note: Salutary neglect's architect: Sir Robert Walpole (with Catherine Shorter), Eccardt after Zinke; 18th-century portrait, covers the 'sleeping dogs' beat.
images.title: Sir Robert Walpole and Catherine Shorter (Eccardt, after Zinke)

images.note: The smuggler-or-not beat: Hancock engraved by Paul Revere, 1774; contemporary, Boston-made, six years after the Liberty seizure.
images.title: The Hon-ble. John Hancock, Esq-r. (Paul Revere Jr., 1774)

images.note: The man who named it: Edmund Burke, who coined 'salutary neglect' in his 1775 speech; drawn by Sergent-Marceau ca. 1815, later depiction.
images.title: Portrait of Edmond Burke (Sergent-Marceau, ca. 1815)

images.note: The demolition's author: Adam Smith, whose 1776 Wealth of Nations attacked 'the whole doctrine of the balance of trade'; Ponscarme medal 1876, later depiction in the Tassie-likeness tradition.
images.title: Adam Smith, Political Economist (Ponscarme medal, 1876)

images.note: Next-episode tease (Great Awakening): George Whitefield, Greenwood after Hone, 1769; contemporary (Hone painted him 1768, a year before his death).
images.title: George Whitefield (John Greenwood after Nathaniel Hone, 1769)
